operations.name: Suggest options from a website
operations.agentTask: Read the website in `sourceUrl` and write three different ways to fill the ad "One hub, three product benefits". Objective: Explain a SaaS or service bundle without presenting a full unreadable dashboard. Visual rule: A single hub remains stable while one benefit card at a time receives attention. Beats, in order: - 0–2 s: Hub and plain-language problem are already visible. Shows Brand color, Hub icon, Problem. - 2–5 s: First card connects to the hub. Shows Brand color, Hub icon, Benefit card 1, Benefit 1. - 5–8 s: Second card replaces the first as focal point. Shows Brand color, Hub icon, Benefit card 2, Benefit 2. - 8–11.5 s: Third card enters; the completed hub becomes visible. Shows Brand color, Hub icon, Benefit card 3, Benefit 3. - 11.5–15 s: Three-card system, outcome and CTA hold together. Shows Brand color, Hub icon, Benefit card 1, Benefit card 2, Benefit card 3, Logo, Outcome and call to action. Use only facts the website or pages you read state. Never invent prices, discounts, dates, guarantees or claims. When a fact a field needs is missing, write a short placeholder in square brackets, such as [offer end date]. Make the three options clearly different in angle, wording and image choice. For images, choose real, large images of this brand and product: first from the page's own images (header logo, large files, feature-page screenshots), then with an image search. A social preview card (og:image, a title on a gradient) is a last resort. Give the direct URL of the image file, never a page URL, and never an image of another brand. Use an empty string when no image fits. If image search throws because no search backend is configured, tell the user in one sentence that a SerpAPI, DataForSEO or Brave key in Settings finds better images. Then take nodetool.web.screenshot of the product's feature pages instead. Save each image you consider as an asset and look at it with view_image before you offer it. Name in the option's description any image that is only a social preview card. Write `fillOptions` as a list of three objects, `fillChoice` as "" and `fillReport` as "". Each option: - value: "1", "2" or "3" - title: a name for the direction in 2 to 4 words - description: one sentence on what it emphasizes, then the first two copy lines in quotes - image: the URL of its first image, for the option card - brandColor: the brand's accent color as #RRGGBB (buttons, links, highlights), not the page background or a theme-color that is near black or white - fields: problem (Problem: hook, at most 7 words); benefit1 (Benefit 1: feature 1, at most 7 words); benefit2 (Benefit 2: feature 2, at most 7 words); benefit3 (Benefit 3: feature 3, at most 7 words); outcomeAndCta (Outcome and call to action: outcome and cta, at most 8 words) - images: hub (Hub icon: An icon or mark on a plain or transparent background. It shows small, as a node or tile, so it must read at about 200 px wide. Not a screenshot or a social preview card. Shown in: Hub and plain-language problem are already visible. | First card connects to the hub. | Second card replaces the first as focal point. | Third card enters; the completed hub becomes visible. | Three-card system, outcome and CTA hold together.); featureCard1 (Benefit card 1: A real photo or screenshot that matches the beats that show it. Shown in: First card connects to the hub. | Three-card system, outcome and CTA hold together.); featureCard2 (Benefit card 2: A real photo or screenshot that matches the beats that show it. Shown in: Second card replaces the first as focal point. | Three-card system, outcome and CTA hold together.); featureCard3 (Benefit card 3: A real photo or screenshot that matches the beats that show it. Shown in: Third card enters; the completed hub becomes visible. | Three-card system, outcome and CTA hold together.); logo (Logo: The brand's own logo file, such as the site header logo or its icon. Shown in: Three-card system, outcome and CTA hold together.) Then show the Start step with `only: ["fillChoice"]` and a one-sentence note, so the user sees just the option cards. Picking one runs `apply`, which saves the images and fills the steps.
